findings.finding: R1-1 is closed in substance. The README now states the unsigned long width of mremap's flags, the low-32-bit compare, and the v6.12 EINVAL for unknown flags at mm/mremap.c:1012-1013, which I checked against the local copy (byte-identical to the upstream file I fetched in round 1, sha256 224327602dbaf82f...). The paraphrase of the model note is imprecise, though. The model actually says 'an int or unsigned int the kernel truncates'. And not every other filtered argument is an int: ioctl arg1, memfd_create arg1, membarrier arg1 and seccomp arg0/arg1 are unsigned int, and clone arg0 is an unsigned long that v6.12 truncates with lower_32_bits (kernel/fork.c:2913-2924, the body x86_64 and arm64 share through CLONE_BACKWARDS). The substantive property (only the low 32 bits reach the kernel's decision for every other filtered argument) holds; I checked all 25 filtered (syscall, arg) pairs. The model docstring was left unchanged, which keeps the model bytes, so its 'every filtered argument' sentence is still literally untrue for mremap; the README now carries the correction.
findings.requiredChange: None for publication. Optionally reword to 'the model's note that every other filtered argument is an int or unsigned int, or (clone flags) an unsigned long the kernel truncates to 32 bits, still holds', and fix the docstring at the next model change.
